identity.author: John Davenant

identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont. (Thomas/Vasquez). Cap. IX Arg. 11 Baptism remains.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont. angel gifts through Thomas/Vasquez.
scope.next_locus: Cap. IX Arg. 11 (Baptism for infants / Corvinus: absolute reprobation makes baptism useless?).

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: angel gifts — God foresaw abuse unto pride and rebellion, yet gifts not subordinated to ruin but to obedience and beatitude
english: Take the angels: God foresaw that some, endowed with excellent gifts, would abuse those gifts in pride and rebellion; he decreed to permit that, and for that rebellion to torment them with everlasting punishments. Yet no one would say those gifts were, by God's primary and proper intention, subordinated to their ruin and damnation — rather to their obedience and beatitude.
sections.latin: Verbi causa; Deus praevidit quosdam Angelos eximiis donis instructos velle iisdem abuti ad superbiendum et rebellandum; decrevit hoc permittere, et propter hanc rebellionem eosdem aeternis suppliciis cruciare: nemo tamen dixerit ea dona ex primaria et propria Dei intentione fuisse ad illorum ruinam et damnationem subordinata, sed potius ad illorum obedientiam et beatitudinem.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: God's intention through means is judged from the nature of the means, not from the evil event he foresaw and would not hinder — same of Gospel gifts to reprobates
english: For — as we warned before — God's intention through means is always judged from the nature of those means, not from the evil event he foresaw and would not hinder. Judge Gospel preaching and the other gifts of divine grace granted to the reprobate the same way.
sections.latin: Nam (quod antea monuimus) intentio Dei per media semper aestimatur ex mediorum natura, et non ex eventu malo, quem Deus praevidet fore, et non vult impedire. Eodem igitur modo de Evangelica praedicatione, aliisque gratiae Divinae muneribus, quae reprobatis conceduntur, sentiendum est.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Remonstrants themselves place preaching under common providence — we grant that, adding special mercy for the elect and permission of contrary effect for the rest
english: The Remonstrants themselves, when it suits them, take Gospel preaching not to flow from some absolute decree to save or damn every hearer, but from a more common providence — what they call Christ's wise, merciful, and just government (Collat. Hagiens. p. 95). Let them then let us subscribe that view, with this added: preaching flows from the predestination decree for those in whom God decreed of special mercy to work penitence, faith, and salvation infallibly through that instrument; and it flows from a more common providence for those in whom he decreed to permit that by their fault it should take a plainly contrary effect — yet we never grant that for these latter it flows from the reprobation decree, or is subordinated as a medium to their damnation by God's primary intention.
sections.latin: Ipsi Remonstrantes intelligunt, quando ex re ipsorum est, praedicationem Evangelii non manare ex absoluto aliquo decreto salvandi aut damnandi omnes et singulos quibus praedicatur, sed ex communiori quadam ratione providentiae, quam illi vocant sapientem, misericordem, et justam Christi gubernationem, Collat. Hagiens. pag. 95. Patiantur igitur et nos illorum sententiae subscribere, hoc addito, Evangelicam praedicationem ex decreto praedestinationis manare quoad illos, in quibus Deus decrevit ex speciali sua misericordia per illud organon poenitentiam, fidem, et salutem infallibiliter operari; Evangelicam autem praedicationem ex communiori quadam providentiae ratione manare quoad illos, in quibus Deus decrevit permittere ut illorum vitio effectum sortiatur plane contrarium; ita tamen ut quoad hosce posteriores ex decreto reprobationis fluere, aut tanquam medium damnationi eorundem primaria Dei intentione subordinatum esse, nullo modo concedamus.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Scripture — Gospel an odor of death from hearers' voluntary rebellion, not from God's primary intention (2 Cor. ii; Heb. ii; Acts xiii; Col. i)
english: Scripture itself settles Gospel preaching far differently: to some it becomes an odor of death unto death (2 Cor. ii. 15–16) — not from God's primary intention, but from their voluntary rebellion (Heb. ii. 3: How shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation?). Acts xiii. 38: Remission of sins through Christ is announced to you — and 46: After you put it from you and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life. Col. i. 28: We announce Christ, admonishing and teaching every one, that we may present every one perfect in Christ Jesus.
sections.latin: Ipsae enim Scripturae de Evangelica praedicatione longe aliter statuunt; fieri nimirum quibusdam odorem mortis ad mortem, 2 Cor. ii. 15, 16. sed non ex primaria Dei intentione, verum ex voluntaria illorum rebellione, Hebr. ii. 3. Quomodo nos effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem? Actor. xiii. 38. Annunciatur vobis remissio peccatorum per Christum, etc. et 46. Postquam repellitis illam, et indignos vos decernitis vita aeterna. Et Coloss. i. 28. Annunciamus Christum, admonentes quosvis, et quosvis erudientes, ut quosvis sistamus perfectos in Christo Jesu.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Gospel not administered from a precise intention of damning anyone — damnation's desert arises from neglect and contempt God foresaw and would not hinder in the reprobate
english: So God does not administer the Gospel to anyone from a nearest precise intention of damning him. When neglect and contempt intervene, desert of damnation arises in the despiser — which God foresaw and was unwilling to hinder in all the reprobate.
sections.latin: Evangelium igitur non administratur ab ipso Deo ulli homini ex proxima et precisa intentione illum damnandi; sed, interveniente ejus neglectu et contemptu, exoritur in contemnente meritum damnationis, quod Deus praevidebat fore, et nolebat impedire in omnibus reprobatis.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: two senses of 'intend' — providence disposing apt means (Adam), and predestination supplying means that secure the end (elect); Arminian third sense of intending evil by the Gospel rejected
english: Finally, to show more clearly the flaw in the denied consequence, add this: we say God 'intends' something in two ways. First, when by providence he disposes apt means toward producing some end — in that sense we say he willed and intended that Adam stand and persevere in obedience to the divine command, because he granted him apt means for standing and persevering. Second, more specially, when by the predestination decree he supplies means by which he knew and decreed the end itself would be obtained — in that sense we say he intended and willed the faith, perseverance, and salvation of all the elect. The third mode the Arminians invent — that God by primary intention wills that evil through Gospel preaching or any benefit granted to men, which will arise from that benefit through the reprobates' malice that God will not hinder — that mode is plainly unheard-of and to be exploded.
sections.latin: Denique, ut vitium negatae consequentiae magis appareat, hoc unum addemus; Deum dici a nobis aliquid intendere dupliciter; uno modo, quando ex providentia disponit apta media ad finis alicujus productionem. Hoc sensu dicimus voluisse atque intendisse Deum ut Adamus in obedientia mandati Divini staret ac perseveraret, quia scilicet concessit illi apta media ad standum et perseverandum. Alio modo et specialiore, quando ex decreto praedestinationis talia media suppeditat, quibus novit et decrevit ipsum finem fore obtinendum. Hoc sensu dicimus Deum intendisse et voluisse fidem, perseverantiam et salutem omnium electorum. Jam vero tertius ille modus, quem fingere conantur Arminiani, ut Deus scilicet dicatur primaria intentione illud malum velle per Evangelicam praedicationem, aut per beneficium quodcunque hominibus concessum, quod ex tali beneficio, mediante reprobatorum malitia, quam Deus non vult impedire, exorietur; hic, inquam, modus est plane inauditus et explodendus.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: means of salvation offered to reprobates are neither effects of predestination nor media of reprobation — they flow from philanthropy and more general providence; Thomas and Vasquez on the distinction
english: So the means of salvation offered to the reprobate are not effects of predestination — else they would reach the end. Nor do they flow from the reprobation decree as media God subordinated to procuring their damnation — for it is not God's part to furnish means that lead reprobates to everlasting death; those sprout abundantly from themselves if he does not oppose special grace. They flow instead from that philanthropy and more general providence which so disposes means toward an end that it meanwhile permits the second cause, by its own fault, to fall short of attaining it. Thomas well explains this distinction between Predestination and Providence (Quaest. Disp. De praed. art. 1); Vasquez acknowledges the same (In 1 q.22 disp. 87 c.4, at the chapter's end).
sections.latin: Media igitur salutis quae offeruntur reprobatis non sunt effectus praedestinationis; quia sic finem consequerentur: neque fluunt a decreto reprobationis, tanquam media ad procurandam reprobatorum damnationem a Deo subordinata; quia non pertinet ad Deum providere de mediis reprobatos ad mortem aeternam ducentibus, quae ex ipsis abunde pullulant, si Deus gratiam specialem non opponat; sed manant ab illa φιλανθρωπίᾳ et generaliore providentia, quae media ad aliquem finem ita disponit, ut interim permittat causam secundam a consecutione finis suo vitio excidere. Hoc discrimen inter Praedestinationem et Providentiam bene explicavit Thomas, Quaest. Disp. De praed. art. 1. Eamque agnoscit ipse Vasques, In 1. quaest. 22. disp. 87. cap. 4. in ipso fine capitis.
